prerequisites: Knowledge of modules KI-1 to KI-12

learning_outcomes.text: explain the challenges of modern autonomous robotics
compile the prerequisites (e.g., sensor technology, actuators) for simple robotics problems
list basic locomotion procedures and compare them
present degrees of freedom of common mobile robot platforms and compare the advantages and disadvantages of these platforms
calculate direct and inverse kinematics of common robot platforms
describe basic path planning and task execution procedures
compare the characteristics of different sensors and estimate their applicability for a simple scenario
calculate error propagation in noisy sensor data
explain localization and map creation fundamentally
present fundamental concepts of Robot Operating System (ROS)
develop a solution for a playful robotics task both in simulation and in the real world
actively search for and study their own solution methods with the help of practical robot tasks

syllabus_topics: Challenges of autonomous mobile robotics and manipulation
Calculation of direct kinematics with Denavit-Hartenberg transformation
Calculation of inverse kinematics with Jacobi matrices
Introduction to Robot Operating System ROS
assessment_rules: The module examination has a duration of 90 minutes. The weighting of the grade is 5/210.
bibliography: Correll, Introduction to Autonomous Robots, 2016, ISBN 0692700870
